analysis:
Examined the head/base of ProviderLoop+Serve.swift and the patch plus base of ProviderLoop+ServingAuthorizationRecovery.swift.

Serve.swift (head lines 429-432): the control-event reader now calls noteCoordinatorRequest() when an .inferenceRequest arrives. This is a local bookkeeping change. The request still goes to workContinuation.yield and through handleInferenceRequest unchanged, so no new data path, no decryption change and no plaintext exposure.

Recovery.swift: noteCoordinatorRequest stamps coordinatorConnection.lastRequestAt only when connected. superviseServingAuthorization now uses ServingReadiness.verdict(connection:trust:now:) instead of hasCurrentAppAttestAuthorization or path=="legacy" combined with UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery.connectionLacksAuthorization. The diff excerpt is truncated and ServingReadiness is not supplied, so the verdict logic is unverified.

Security relevance (T-052, T-053, T-057): this supervision is local and diagnostic. It logs and decides whether to re-register (requestPlannedReconnect) a connection the coordinator keeps refusing. It does not grant serving authorization. The coordinator still authorizes and revokes, and handleTrustStatus / clearConnectionAuthorization are unchanged. A coordinator-routed request being treated as newer evidence than an earlier refusal can only suppress or clear the reconnect timer (unauthorizedSince=nil) and does not enable serving. A hostile or buggy coordinator is outside the trust model here, since it is trusted. A consumer cannot forge inferenceRequest events, because they arrive over the authenticated coordinator socket.

The .pending, .unconfirmed and nil cases reset unauthorizedSince without reconnecting. This could reduce self-healing recovery if the verdict mislabels a state (availability only, T-057). The old code also treated the legacy path as authorized, and whether ServingReadiness preserves that is not visible.

Open questions for the integration pass: ServingReadiness.verdict semantics (stale blocked vs lastRequestAt ordering), the DaemonState.CoordinatorConnection.lastRequestAt persistence and any consumers such as status/doctor, and whether lastRequestAt is reset on reconnect (noteCoordinatorConnection creates a fresh struct, so it is). No concrete regression is identified in the supplied evidence.
